headline: Bangladesh lose to India by 40 runs, bow out of Women's Asia Cup
summary: A disappointing effort in all three departments ends Bangladesh's campaign in the regional competition after a semifinal defeat in Dubai.
details: Bangladesh's Women's team lost to India by 40 runs in the first semifinal of the Women's Asia Cup T20 in Dubai on Thursday, ending their journey in the tournament.
India posted a competitive 149 for six after being asked to bat first. While Bangladesh kept them in check until the 15th over, India added 53 runs in the final five overs to reach the total.
Shafali Verma top-scored for India with 64 off 40 balls, while Harmanpreet Kaur and Richa Ghosh provided crucial late impetus.
In response, Bangladesh's chase struggled from the start. The batters focused more on avoiding a heavy defeat than pursuing the 150-run target, finishing on 109 for seven in their 20 overs.
Shorna Akter remained unbeaten on 22 off 18 balls, but the match had already slipped away. Top-order batters and skipper Nigar Sultana Joty failed to convert their starts.
This marks Bangladesh's ninth consecutive T20I loss to India, a streak dating back to September 2023. India now advances to the final to face either Sri Lanka or Pakistan.
The seven-time champions India will play the final on Sunday at the same venue in Dubai.
caption:
9 consecutive T20I losses to India. Bangladesh's Women's team bows out of the Asia Cup after a 40-run semifinal defeat.

Bangladesh's Women's team lost to India by 40 runs in the first semifinal of the Women's Asia Cup T20 in Dubai on Thursday, ending their journey in the tournament.

India posted a competitive 149 for six after being asked to bat first. While Bangladesh kept them in check until the 15th over, India added 53 runs in the final five overs to reach the total.

Shafali Verma top-scored for India with 64 off 40 balls, while Harmanpreet Kaur and Richa Ghosh provided crucial late impetus.

In response, Bangladesh's chase struggled from the start. The batters focused more on avoiding a heavy defeat than pursuing the 150-run target, finishing on 109 for seven in their 20 overs.

Shorna Akter remained unbeaten on 22 off 18 balls, but the match had already slipped away. Top-order batters and skipper Nigar Sultana Joty failed to convert their starts.

This marks Bangladesh's ninth consecutive T20I loss to India, a streak dating back to September 2023. India now advances to the final to face either Sri Lanka or Pakistan.

The seven-time champions India will play the final on Sunday at the same venue in Dubai.

headline: 70 foreign nationals detained in Chittagong for illegal casino
summary: Police raided an eight-story building in Khulshi, uncovering an illegal casino operation involving citizens of Laos, China, Pakistan, and Vietnam.
details: Police conducted a raid on an eight-story building in the West Jalalabad area of Khulshi, Chittagong, on Thursday afternoon.
The operation targeted an illegal casino operation, resulting in the detention of 70 foreign nationals.
The detainees include citizens of Laos, China, Pakistan, and Vietnam, who are currently being questioned by law enforcement.
During the raid, police recovered over 50 laptops, various foreign currencies, and equipment used to operate the casino.
Local residents reported that foreigners had been frequently visiting the building for about a month.
Police are now investigating the identity of the detainees and the legality of their stay in Bangladesh.
caption:
70 foreign nationals detained in a single raid! An illegal casino uncovered in Chittagong.

Police conducted a raid on an eight-story building in the West Jalalabad area of Khulshi, Chittagong, on Thursday afternoon.

The operation targeted an illegal casino operation, resulting in the detention of 70 foreign nationals.

The detainees include citizens of Laos, China, Pakistan, and Vietnam, who are currently being questioned by law enforcement.

During the raid, police recovered over 50 laptops, various foreign currencies, and equipment used to operate the casino.

Local residents reported that foreigners had been frequently visiting the building for about a month.

Police are now investigating the identity of the detainees and the legality of their stay in Bangladesh.
